transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… work, mostly. There’s a new operations manager, and he’s been picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. I thought I was handling it, but I’m not really leaving it there anymore. I come home tense, snap at my husband, lie awake going over meetings, and then at work I’m second-guessing calls I used to make without thinking.
Do you find yourself constantly thinking about these inspection procedures and the operations manager's criticisms outside of work?

Yes… I do. I try not to, but it follows me home. I keep replaying what he said about my procedures, wondering if I missed something, and then the next day I’m not as sure about calls I’ve made for years.
Have you been avoiding certain tasks or situations at work since the new operations manager started criticizing your procedures?

Yeah… I guess I have. I’ve pulled back from some meetings I’m supposed to be in, and I’m slower getting things done, so I’ve missed some internal deadlines. It’s not like me.

And at home… things are tense. My husband and I argue more, and I’m not really keeping up with our usual evening stuff like I used to.
Do you feel anxious when you're not thinking about work or the operations manager's criticisms?
Not really in the same way. It’s mostly tied to work… to him picking apart my procedures. When I’m not thinking about that, I can settle a little, but it doesn’t take much for it to come back.
Do you feel like you're unable to control these thoughts about the inspection procedures and the operations manager's criticisms?

Yeah… it feels that way. I can tell myself to stop thinking about it, but then I’m home and I’m still replaying what was said in meetings or wondering if I did something wrong with a procedure I’ve used for years. It’s hard to shut off.
Have you been avoiding social gatherings or events outside of work since the new operations manager started?
I… don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t really noticed avoiding things outside of work. It’s more… work stuff that gets to me.
Do you have thoughts that repeat over and over in your mind that you try to ignore or suppress?
Yeah… mostly about work. I try not to think about what he said in meetings or whether I messed up some inspection call, but it just keeps coming back. Even at home, I’ll catch myself replaying it.
Have you noticed any impact on your relationship with your husband beyond just being tense or arguing more?

A little, yeah. It’s not just the arguing… I’m not really keeping up with our usual evenings like I used to. Things I’d normally do around the house or with him, I just… let them slide. It’s been hard on us.
Do you feel like your tension and worries about work are significantly affecting your overall quality of life?

Yeah… I think it is. I don’t really like saying that, but my work record’s been affected. I’ve missed some internal deadlines, and I’ve been pulling back from meetings I’m supposed to be in. And at home… my husband and I argue more, and I’m not really keeping up with our usual evenings like I used to.
Do you have thoughts that are intrusive or unwanted, and that you try to ignore or suppress, outside of those related to work or the operations manager's criticisms?
No… I don’t think so. Not really outside of work stuff. At least, nothing that stands out to me.
Do you often feel anxious when you are not thinking about work or the operations manager's criticisms?
Not really… I mean, I can get a little uneasy in general, but it mostly comes back to work when I think about it. I haven’t noticed it much otherwise.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the time since the new operations manager started criticizing your procedures?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say sad or depressed most of the time. More worn down, maybe. I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the day, nearly every day, since the new operations manager started?
I don’t think it’s been like… sad or empty most of the day, every day. I’ve felt pretty worn out by it, but I wouldn’t put it that way.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed for most of the day?
Not most of the day, no. I mean… I have low moments, but I wouldn’t say it’s like that most of the time.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your sleep pattern since the new operations manager started criticizing your procedures?
Yeah… somewhat. I’ve been lying awake more, replaying things from work in my head. It’s like I come home still wound up, and then I don’t settle down easily.
Do you feel sad or depressed most of the time?
Not most of the time, no. I get down sometimes, but… I wouldn’t say it’s most of the time.
Do you often feel anxious when you are not thinking about work or the operations manager's criticisms?
I’m not really sure. I don’t notice it as much if work isn’t on my mind… but I can’t say for certain.
Do you feel anxious when you're doing things you normally enjoy?
I don’t really know. I haven’t paid close attention to that… I guess if I’m distracted enough, it’s not as noticeable.
Do you feel anxious when you are engaged in activities that you normally find relaxing or enjoyable?
I’m not sure. I guess sometimes I can still relax a little if I’m focused on something else, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m anxious then.
Do you feel anxious most of the time, even when you're not thinking about work?

Not most of the time, I don’t think. It’s more… when work gets in my head. Since the new operations manager started criticizing how I do inspections, I come home wound up and have trouble shutting it off. Even the next day, I start doubting routine calls I used to make without thinking.
